doc.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: First Washington engagement with Carmen Leggio
summary: A year later he played a Washington club for thirteen weeks with Carmen Leggio's group near the Howard Theater, then Rick Henderson hired him and Earl Bostic heard him.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: It didn’t take you too long before you started playing out.

I was going out a year later. The next year I went down to Washington. A saxophone player from White Plains, Carmen Leggio, had been stationed down there in the service. And when he got out he used to go jam at this club. And the lady said, “if you can get a group together I’d like for you to come in.” So he brought a drummer from Tarrytown, and a piano player from New Rochelle and myself. And we came down there, you know, green. First time away from home, we got out and the whole bit. And we came in for four weeks and stayed thirteen weeks. We were right around the corner from the Howard Theater and then around the corner was two other clubs, and Benny Golson was at Howard University then, and he was working at the club, and Ed Jones who later went on to Basie, and Charlie Rouse and Jimmy Cobb, and you know, the whole — so we spent thirteen weeks and then we went back the next year and did eight weeks. And then a © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

saxophone player named Rick Henderson called me in December to see if I could come down and do a month with him in January at a club down there, sort of like a supper club, and then Bostic came to town and heard me and asked me did I want to go with him, and that’s how it went on.
